description: Between **1966** and **1976**, **Mao Zedong** launches a purge of extreme violence to regain power. Red Guards, chaos, then pragmatic turn by **Deng Xiaoping**.

hero.hook: When a head of state calls on youth to destroy his own party.

blocks.text: Between **1966** and **1976**, China went through one of the darkest periods in its modern history: the Cultural Revolution. **Mao Zedong**, founder of the People's Republic and leader of the Communist Party, did not launch a reform there. He launches a purge to regain absolute power.
By mobilizing youth against the state and society, it provokes the persecution of tens of millions of people and the destruction of an immense part of Chinese heritage.

Everything starts from the failure of  (**1958-1962**): forced collectivization, famine, millions of deaths, Mao's prestige shaken. More pragmatic leaders, like  (President of the Republic) and , are taking the economy in hand. **[[The Great Leap Forward (1958-1962)]]** **[[Liu Shaoqi]]** **[[Deng Xiaoping]]**

blocks.caption: Mao Zedong, the “Great Helmsman”, at the center of the cult of personality.

blocks.text: Mao bypasses the Party. In **1966**, his  (wall poster) “Bomb the headquarters” accuses the leaders of being “revisionists”. The head of state declares war on his own administration. **[[Dazibao]]**
At age 72, Mao swims in the Yangtze in July **1966**. The propaganda claims an impossible record of 15 km in 65 minutes: proof that he is “combat ready”.

sections.title: After the failure of the Great Leap

blocks.text: Millions of high school and college students form the . Mission: destroy the “four old things” (ideas, culture, customs, habits). Their bible: the Little Red Book, a collection of quotes from Mao. **[[The Red Guards]]**

blocks.caption: Red Guards brandishing the Little Red Book.

blocks.text: Humiliated teachers, executives dragged into the street, schools closed: ideological “purity” takes precedence over everything. Wearing Western clothing or a foreign book can be expensive.
In Beijing, Red Guards tried to make the red light the signal to “pass,” because red was the revolutionary color.

sections.title: The fury of the Red Guards

blocks.text: From **1967**, the Red Guard factions are killing each other. Mao brought in the , the Chinese army, and sent **17 million** young urban people to “re-educate” themselves in the countryside. **[[People's Liberation Army]]**

At the top, the struggle for succession pitted the radicals of the , including , Mao's wife, against the survivors of the purges. The death of Mao, **September 9, 1976**, then the arrest of the **[[Gang of Four]]**, closed the decade of chaos. **[[Jiang Qing]]**

The human toll is estimated between **500,000** and **2 million** direct deaths, not counting broken lives. In **1981**, the Party recognizes a “serious error”, while preserving Mao as father of the nation.
, twice purged, imposes economic openness: “It doesn't matter whether the cat is white or black, as long as it catches mice. » China is moving from class struggle to growth. **[[Deng Xiaoping]]**
